claims.text: The mechanical properties of HfNbTaTiZr HEA can be predicted and understood by combining controlled-variable experiments with atomistic simulations.
Changing the percentage of an individual HfNbTaTiZr constituent affects the alloy's microstructure and crystal structure.
Microstructure and crystal structure affect the deformation mechanisms of HfNbTaTiZr HEA.
Changes in deformation mechanisms alter the mechanical behavior of HfNbTaTiZr HEA.
Strength, ductility, and hardness will change predictably as the percentages of Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, or Zr are varied.
The relevant composition range is bounded by the solubility and stability limits of the constituent elements.
Tensile testing, compression testing, and nanoindentation can be used to evaluate mechanical-property changes caused by systematic compositional variation.
The exact direction and magnitude of each constituent element's effect are currently uncertain.
